What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/backup.zip and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Public-Facing Security Exposure Checks behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/.git/logs/HEAD and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Advanced Git Repository Exposure & Directory Listing behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/ and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether CSRF – God Level (Token Absence + Form Detection) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/ and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Missing Security Headers behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
Recommended protection

Add the missing security headers appropriate to your application's context.

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/swagger.json and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Advanced Mass Assignment & Prototype Pollution behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/.env and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Bug-Bounty Environment Exposure (Cloud, K8s, Vault) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • A user may access another user's object or record.
  • Private information may be exposed.
  • The attacker may be able to modify data if the endpoint allows changes.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/users and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether BOLA - Uncommon Vectors (Wildcards, Arrays, Overrides, Cache) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • A production API could expose another user's records or objects.
  • The risk is especially important when the affected data contains private or sensitive information.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/backup.zip and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Public-Facing Security Exposure Checks behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/.git/logs/HEAD and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Advanced Git Repository Exposure & Directory Listing behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/ and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether CSRF – God Level (Token Absence + Form Detection) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/ and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Missing Security Headers behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/swagger.json and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Advanced Mass Assignment & Prototype Pollution behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/.env and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Bug-Bounty Environment Exposure (Cloud, K8s, Vault) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • A user may access another user's object or record.
  • Private information may be exposed.
  • The attacker may be able to modify data if the endpoint allows changes.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/users and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether BOLA - Uncommon Vectors (Wildcards, Arrays, Overrides, Cache) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • A production API could expose another user's records or objects.
  • The risk is especially important when the affected data contains private or sensitive information.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://github.com/sidekiq and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Public-Facing Security Exposure Checks behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://github.com/ and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether CSRF – God Level (Token Absence + Form Detection) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://github.com/profile and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Advanced CSRF Misconfiguration (CORS Chain + Token Reuse) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What can go wrong?

  • A user may access another user's object or record.
  • Private information may be exposed.
  • The attacker may be able to modify data if the endpoint allows changes.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://github.com/profile and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether BOLA - Uncommon Vectors (Wildcards, Arrays, Overrides, Cache) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • A production API could expose another user's records or objects.
  • The risk is especially important when the affected data contains private or sensitive information.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • Attackers may influence database queries.
  • Sensitive records may become accessible.
  • Authentication or application logic may be bypassed.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://github.com/login and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Advanced NoSQL Injection behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • A production application could expose or manipulate database-backed information.
  • The final impact depends on the database permissions available to the application.
  • Because the finding is rated critical severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://github.com/sidekiq and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Public-Facing Security Exposure Checks behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://github.com/server-status and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Bug-Bounty Environment Exposure (Cloud, K8s, Vault) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://github.com/ and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether CSRF – God Level (Token Absence + Form Detection) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://github.com/profile and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Advanced CSRF Misconfiguration (CORS Chain + Token Reuse) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • A user may access another user's object or record.
  • Private information may be exposed.
  • The attacker may be able to modify data if the endpoint allows changes.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://github.com/profile and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether BOLA - Uncommon Vectors (Wildcards, Arrays, Overrides, Cache) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • A production API could expose another user's records or objects.
  • The risk is especially important when the affected data contains private or sensitive information.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • Attackers may influence database queries.
  • Sensitive records may become accessible.
  • Authentication or application logic may be bypassed.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://github.com/login and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Advanced NoSQL Injection behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • A production application could expose or manipulate database-backed information.
  • The final impact depends on the database permissions available to the application.
  • Because the finding is rated critical severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.

  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://onlinekhabar.com/.env and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Public-Facing Security Exposure Checks behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://onlinekhabar.com/.env and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Bug-Bounty Environment Exposure (Cloud, K8s, Vault) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.

  • The risk is especially important when the affected data contains private or sensitive information.

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://onlinekhabar.com/ and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Advanced SSRF Detection behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
  • Because the finding is rated critical severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • Attackers may influence database queries.
  • Sensitive records may become accessible.
  • Authentication or application logic may be bypassed.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://onlinekhabar.com/login and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Advanced NoSQL Injection behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • A production application could expose or manipulate database-backed information.
  • The final impact depends on the database permissions available to the application.
  • Because the finding is rated critical severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://onlinekhabar.com/.env and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Public-Facing Security Exposure Checks behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.

What can go wrong?

  • The weakness may allow behaviour the application did not intend.
  • The actual impact depends on server configuration and permissions.
  • A manual security review should confirm the final impact.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://onlinekhabar.com/.env and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Bug-Bounty Environment Exposure (Cloud, K8s, Vault) behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • The same behaviour on a production system could expose data or functionality to unauthorized users.
  • The final impact must be confirmed against the application's actual permissions and data.
  • Because the finding is rated high severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.

What is this?

This is what the server returned after receiving the request. VulnForge uses this information as evidence when deciding whether the tested behaviour is suspicious.

What is this?

The request is what VulnForge sent. The response is what the server returned. Together they form the main evidence for this finding.

What can go wrong?

  • Attackers may influence database queries.
  • Sensitive records may become accessible.
  • Authentication or application logic may be bypassed.

What did VulnForge test?

VulnForge sent a controlled test to GET https://onlinekhabar.com/login and examined how the application responded. The goal was to determine whether Advanced NoSQL Injection behaves in a way that matches the security weakness detected by the scanner.

Real-world impact

  • A production application could expose or manipulate database-backed information.
  • The final impact depends on the database permissions available to the application.
  • Because the finding is rated critical severity, it should be reviewed before relying on the affected endpoint in production.
Recommended protection

Review the affected endpoint, apply the appropriate server-side security control, and retest the endpoint.
